text:
incident-bot: ALERT: prod:streaming p99 latency > 12s for shard-group-A. SLO breach triggered. Escalating to oncall.
jeff: Ack. I'm on it — looking at dashboards. p95 ~2.3s, p99 jumping 12-18s. Streaming stalls and some tail timeouts showing.
dave: Looking at the infra metrics: `kv_cache_eviction_rate` is through the roof, and `swap_io` on the NVMe devices is high. Prefill vs decode ratio is skewed — prefill ops >> decode ops.
sam: host-level IO looks bad. `iostat` shows write latency spikes. Could be KV fragmentation causing frequent evictions -> thrash -> decode misses -> tail spikes.
jeff: Customer impact: org-347 and org-912 report streaming stalls/timeouts ~10-15s. Support looped in @maria. Potential SLA exposure.
maria: Confirmed. Both customers opened support tickets. No data integrity issues. Messaging prepared: "We've applied mitigations; performance improving; next update in 30m."
dave: Quick root hypothesis: long-context prefill entries not being chunked; they create large KV entries that evict many smaller, hotter keys. This increases decode cache misses and creates tail latency. Also compaction not keeping up so fragmentation rises.
jeff: Fast mitigations I can try: 1) reduce `prefill_batch_size` 64->16 on group-A 2) flip `prefer_hot_eviction` to true 3) route non-critical streaming to fallback pool-B. Thoughts? :thinking_face:
sam: I can flip `prefer_hot_eviction` and put a routing rule to throttle low-priority streams. Reducing prefill batch will shift CPU, so monitor p95.
dave: Also recommend temporary `decode_first` heuristic: give decode path higher cache priority so decode hits aren't evicted by large prefill entries. Flag: `runtime.kv.decode_priority=true`. Should run in canary first.
jeff: Ok. Plan: Sam, flip eviction toggle + route rule. Dave, enable `decode_priority` in canary. I'll reduce prefill batch on the group once we see canary numbers.
sam: Applying eviction toggle now. Pushing route rule to send `streaming.debug=false` -> pool-B. ETA ~30s.
deploy-bot: Route rule update: id=r_20260315_01 applied to edge (3 replicas).
sam: Eviction toggle applied on shard-A hosts. Observability: `kv_cache_eviction_rate` down ~40% within 2m. `swap_io` decreasing. p99 trending from 16s -> ~6s.
dave: Enabled `runtime.kv.decode_priority=true` on a canary (2 hosts). Canary p99 -> 3.2s, streaming stalls drop off. Rolling to remaining hosts now.
jeff: Nice. Maria — please send the customer update: short note that we've applied mitigations and are monitoring; will follow up with postmortem.
maria: Sent to org-347 & org-912. They acknowledged, asking for ETA on root cause.
jeff: Next steps / action items: * dave -> open RFC for KV compaction + chunking prefill entries * sam -> add host-level swap thresholds and automated eviction throttle * infra -> consider proactive compaction job during low traffic windows * jeff -> schedule incident review and link eval prompt set for regression tests.
dave: Also capturing quick log snippet that showed eviction thrash pattern:
```
[2026-03-15T12:12:03Z] kv: evict key=ctx:long:abcd len=1.2MB cause=memory_pressure
[2026-03-15T12:12:03Z] kv: evict key=session:hot:37 len=8KB cause=memory_pressure
[2026-03-15T12:12:04Z] cache: miss decode key=session:hot:37 -> backend decode path latency+=180ms
```
jeff: Handoff: Lina, I'm handing off monitoring and follow-up to you for the next shift. Summary: mitigations applied (hot-eviction toggle, decode_priority, routing fallback to pool-B, prefill batch reduction pending). Watch p99 and swap_io; if p99 > 8s escalate.
lina: Taking over. Quick checklist received. I'll watch the dashboards (`/dashboards/kv_eviction`, `/dashboards/streaming_tail`) and check logs every 10m. If we see repeat evictions/fragmentation, I'll start immediate compaction job in maintenance window.
jeff: Thanks — I'll remain reachable. Marking incident as acknowledged and monitoring. :white_check_mark:
lina: Acknowledged. I'll post an incident recap and action items after 30m of stable metrics.
